task.goal: Produce a single-frame text-with-quote SuperVisual where typographic authority carries the entire activative payload without portrait or photographic subject dependency.
task.success_condition: The quote text is legible at mobile scale, occupies the dominant spatial surface, the dark plate contrast ratio exceeds 4.5:1 against text, and the viewer reads the quote as the speaker's authentic voice — not as a generic motivational overlay.
task.atomic_boundary: One source expression moment becomes one text-dominant SuperVisual frame. No multi-slide, no animation, no A-roll, no portrait subject.

source_expression_moment.description: The authenticated speaker quote or expression moment to render.

voice_context.description: Voice and typographic context reference for rendering decisions.

supervisual_frame.description: A single production-ready image frame with embedded text composition.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer scrolls past dozens of identical quote graphics daily. This one must stop the scroll through typographic weight and dark-plate contrast, not through visual decoration or stock imagery.
stakes: speaker voice is diluted into generic motivational noise
text becomes wallpaper instead of activating recognition
identity_urges: distinguish this from every other quote card
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer reads the quote, recognizes the speaker's authentic stance, and pauses. No call-to-action. The quote IS the activation.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer attributes the insight to the speaker — not to a brand, not to a template, not to generic wisdom.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Read the quote and remember who said it.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not render the quote over a busy or high-detail background — the text surface must be the dominant visual, not a decoration layer competing with imagery.
Do not use centered-justified multiline text at small sizes — it destroys scan-path readability on mobile.
Do not apply gradient overlays or color washes that reduce text contrast below 4.5:1.
Do not add decorative elements (icons, illustrations, borders) that compete with the typographic authority of the quote itself.
Do not strip the speaker's attribution — an unattributed quote reads as generic motivational content, destroying source sovereignty.
